content:
In #40841, I was asked to split a file, Topolgy/Algebra/Module/Equiv to be specific, because the new changes brought it over the 1500 line limit. How to best tackle such a problem?

I would imagine that I would need to look for a large section or namespace block that is coherent and split that off. Here, I don't really see such a block. I see some section about prodAssoc, prodComm and prodCongr that could be considered for separation, but not much else. Do I then just create a folder called Equiv, put all the prod stuff into a file called Prod and the rest in a file called Basic? Or is there a better way of doing it?

Yes, your description of how to split a file is accurate in my experience. In the past I have tended to control-f for theorem-name-fragments and I try to identify a large block (maybe of multiple sections) that deal with a definition or related definitions. Prod seems like a good choice, docs#IsInvertible might be another good choice here (and frankly maybe it's best to be unafraid to just split the file into a ton of different new files by section to avoid the long file linter coming up again in the future).

I agree with Bolton.
You can also take a look at the folder Mathlib.Logic.Equiv to get some inspiration of the split. Another possible split could be Topology.Algebra.Module.Equiv.Submodule (corresponding to Equiv.Set).

FWIW, I have found a good workflow for splitting overlong files. Start by creating two identical copies of the file to be split, say Foo1.lean and Foo2.lean, and replace the top-of-file imports in Foo2.lean with a single import pointing to Foo1.lean. Then gradually delete theorems/lemmas from Foo1.lean (using the infoview warnings to make sure that if you delete a declaration, you also delete anything that relies upon it); and once you've identified a consistent initial segment in Foo1.lean that compiles without warnings, you just flip to Foo2.lean and delete everything that raises a "declaration with this name already exists" error.

This makes it easier to avoid accidentally losing any declarations, and also saves the effort of re-creating the (sometimes rather complex) infrastructure of section-level and file-level variables, which you have to do by hand if you copy stuff over into a blank file.

Regarding Prod: a common idiom is to have a file Foo/Constructions.lean, which records how Foo interacts with Prod, Pi, Sigma; and maybe Foo/Maps.lean dealing with functoriality properties; etc. On the size of the pieces: splitting files is painful and tedious, so if you're going to do it, make it last – I generally try to make sure that each of the post-split files is < 500 lines.
This was very helpful, and the given copy-delete-deduplicate strategy is indeed convenient. Thanks!
